title: Deferred features are rejected with generic or wrong diagnostics, not structured unsupported diagnostics
Sized numeric types other than i64 (i8, i16, u8-u64, f32) are unimplemented and not listed as deferred
Embedding simplification cannot be fully exercised: the prototype compiles one module without trait imports, so trait availability is untested, and the fixtures need package roles
Visibility-aware member lookup cannot be exercised: the prototype compiles one module, so every own member is visible, and the fixtures need package roles
Literal suffixes (L1-L9) work for library suffix types, but `std.time` is not declared, because its `Duration` and suffix newtypes need `i64`
`std.format.Debug` is not implemented: `@derive(Debug)` is accepted and every type counts as `Debug`, but there is no `debug` function or `DebugWriter` (Testing T33, T39, T48)
The prototype binds `Console` as an opaque host provider, not a prelude trait, so `Console.write_line!(mut self)` cannot be called on `mut Console` or implemented
Trait-argument ownership fixtures need the `Iterable` trait or package roles, which the prototype lacks
Entry-point cases use a private declaration in `pub fn main`, so they also report `private-type-leak`
`std.process.ExitCode` and `Termination` are not declared, because the prototype has no `u8` (Testing T8)
The `disposed-file` runtime profile named in spec/conformance/README.md does not exist
The prototype has no pack operations, so `pack.map(` on a local named `pack` resolves as a method call
`annotate` declarations do not parse, so an annotation body holding only an indented `pass` fails
`std.testing.snapshot_file` is not implemented; `snapshot` is checked as a string `assert_equal` (Testing T49)
